subject: Next Steps: Dedicated deployment & integration roadmap (Helix Health)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodai.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodai.com>

Subject: Re: Demo Recap — next steps for Dedicated

Thanks again for your time today, Sarah and Michael — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can move toward a Dedicated proposal that matches Helix’s needs.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sku-estimate.pdf, integration-checklist.xlsx

Recap (high level)
- Goal: Replace current hosted inference for PHI-adjacent features with Redwood Dedicated in our VPC (customer-managed). Primary drivers: latency predictability, data separation, and auditability.
- Primary workloads: clinical-note generation for careflows and embeddings-based similarity search for patient records.
- Expected traffic profile (you mentioned): peaks during batch jobs and daytime surge for real-time lookups.

Action items / questions for Helix (please confirm):
1) Traffic & performance targets: can you share SLOs for 95th percentile inference latency and QPS/requests-per-minute during peak? Also average request size (tokens) and typical session lengths.
2) Concurrency footprint: How many concurrent users will hit the clinical-note generation endpoint versus embeddings/rerank? Any rough per-minute concurrency expectations would help.
3) Auth & networking: Will you be using mTLS between Redwood and your VPC, or would you prefer API-key + IP allowlist initially? Any KMS/HSM integration requirements?
4) Integrations: Do you need structured tool-calling / function outputs for downstream pipelines (we demoed tool-calling). For embeddings we recommend an initial vector size and candidate re-ranker approach — want to confirm expected recall targets.
5) Procurement timeline: Is there a required procurement/PO lead time or an internal date you’re targeting for cutover?

What we’ll prepare (Redwood):
- A dedicated sizing proposal (GPU SKUs, baseline + burst capacity) and cost estimate (attached).
- Integration checklist with SDK snippets for auth, routing rules, and best-practice batching/prefix caching (attached).
- Autoscaling and canary cutover plan (policy + rollback criteria).

Proposed next steps:
- You: send traffic profile CSV and procurement contact (cc added if helpful).
- Us: draft Dedicated proposal and a short technical design doc for the integration.
- Schedule: can we do a technical deep-dive with your infra/SRE on Thurs 3/26? Please share preferred time windows.

Thanks — I’ll loop in our SEs to scope the technical design once we have your traffic shapes.

—

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with our expectations. A few quick answers and attachments to get you started.

Answers:
- SLOs: Target 95th token latency of ~200ms for short-generation endpoints (<=128 tokens). For longer note generation (avg ~450 tokens) we’re OK with up to 1s tail.
- Traffic: daytime peak ~120 reqs/min for real-time lookups, background batch jobs spike ~2k requests over 15–30 minute windows. Concurrency: peak concurrent requests ~35 across services.
- Auth: we prefer mTLS for the production VPC deployment; for pilot we can start with API-key + IP allowlist. We do use AWS KMS and would want CMKs for any encryption keys you store.
- Structured output: yes — we need tool-calling for a ‘patient-facts’ extractor and structured JSON outputs for downstream validation.
- Procurement: our procurement team prefers receiving an itemized estimate; we can sign in April if terms look reasonable.

Attached: helix-traffic-patterns.csv (coming in a separate email from our infra team), procurement_contact.txt

We’re available for a technical deep-dive Thurs 3/26 afternoon PT. I’ll let Procurements propose a time.

Folks — forwarding Sarah’s answers and the ask. Summary of what we need from SE/solutions: please prepare a draft Dedicated proposal and a short technical runbook before Thurs 3/26 deep-dive. Key requirements to include:

1) Sizing / throughput: Recommend GPU SKUs and node counts to meet these targets: 95th token latency ~200ms (<=128 tokens) and handling peaks (120 reqs/min real-time, 2k batch spike). Include baseline + burst (burst window ~30m) and expected concurrency headroom.
2) Autoscaling policy: suggested thresholds (CPU/GPU utilization, queue length), cooldowns, and warm-start strategy for KV cache to avoid cold-start latency.
3) Concurrency & queues: per-GPU concurrent streams estimate (tokens/second), recommended queue size/length to preserve tail latency, and backpressure behavior. Also propose a graceful degradation plan (fallback to a smaller quantized model variant).
4) SDK/auth examples: short snippet for our Node SDK showing mTLS handshake + token fallback; also an example routing policy to split embeddings vs. generation traffic.
5) Structured output/tool-calling: template for JSON schema enforcement and a suggested re-ranker approach for embeddings+rerank (initial recall target: 90% top-5).
6) Attachable deliverables: one-pager estimate (cost), technical runbook (3–4 pages) with sample requests, and a cutover checklist for the canary.

Timing: can we have an internal draft by EOD Wed 3/25 so Jordan and I can review before the external deep-dive?

Appreciate it — Laura, Vivek, if you have specific constraints from an offering/SLA perspective please flag.

Subject: Re: Next Steps: Dedicated deployment & integration roadmap (Helix Health)

Thanks — Jordan and Sarah. Per Jordan’s request, attached is a concise proposal and the technical runbook draft. High-level summary below; please let me know if you want different trade-offs.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf, integration-checklist.xlsx

Sizing (recommendation)
- Workloads: split into two service classes: real-time generation (short requests, <=128 tokens) and long-generation/batch (avg ~450 tokens). Embeddings handled by a dedicated pool for vectorization + re-rank.
- Baseline cluster: 4x A10G-equivalent nodes for real-time generation (expect ~12 concurrent real-time streams per GPU with ~150ms mean token latency given batching config). This meets 95th ~200ms for <=128 tokens at 120 req/min with conservative batching.
- Batch/long-gen pool: 2x A10G-equivalent nodes scaled during batch windows; allow burst to 6 nodes for the 30-minute spike.
- Embeddings pool: 2x T4-equivalent nodes (vectorization parallelism) with autoscale to 4 for spikes.

Autoscaling policy (suggested)
- Real-time pool: scale-out trigger when 95th token latency > 180ms OR GPU util > 70% for 2 consecutive minutes. Scale step: +1 node; cooldown 3 minutes.
- Burst policy: allow scheduled burst window (customers specify expected batch windows) to temporarily override scale limits and allow +50% capacity for 30 minutes.
- Warm-start: keep at least 1 standby node warmed with model KV cache preloaded during business hours to avoid cold-start penalties.

Concurrency, batching, and queues
- Per-GPU concurrent streams: estimate 10–14 concurrent short-generation streams per GPU depending on average sequence length and batch window.
- Batching: enable micro-batching up to 32 tokens per batch and prefer prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce compute.
- Queueing/backpressure: soft queue threshold of 150 requests; when exceeded, return 429 with Retry-After and route low-priority requests to a lower-cost quantized model.

Fallback and graceful degradation
- Primary fallback: route overflow to a quantized 8-bit model variant (slightly lower quality) with similar API surface.
- Secondary fallback: route to hosted Redwood endpoint if Dedicated capacity depleted (requires explicit routing policy consent).

Auth & SDK snippets (summary)
- Pilot: API-key + IP allowlist. Production: mTLS with mutual client certs; KMS integration for CMK and envelope keys.
- Node snippet (included in runbook): mTLS handshake sample + automatic token refresh, and client-side routing logic for embeddings vs. generation.

Structured output / tool-calling
- Provide JSON schema enforcement at the response layer; reject and log schema mismatches for eval.
- Recommend a two-stage rerank: sparse candidate retrieval -> dense embed reorder -> lightweight cross-attention re-ranker for top-10. Target top-5 recall >= 90% in initial tuning.

Deliverables and next steps
- Deliverables: redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf (cost + SKU), technical-runbook-draft (attached xlsx), SDK snippets Gist link (in runbook).
- Proposed call: Thurs 3/26 1:00–2:00 PM PT for technical deep-dive (please confirm).
- Procurement: Jordan, Laura — we can produce a formal quote once procurement returns PO terms.

If this looks good I’ll finalize and add the explicit autoscale knobs (GPU mem thresholds, cache warm percentages) in the runbook by EOD 3/25 so you have everything for the call.
